page: UpCloud STARTER-4xCPU-16GB is a virtual server instance categorized in the Starter family, operating on the KVM hypervisor. It is configured with 4 shared vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9575F processor clocked at 2.0 GHz, supporting the x86_64 architecture. The CPU configuration exposes an instruction set that includes AVX-512 extensions (AVX-512F, AVX-512_VNNI, AVX-512_BF16) and cryptographic acceleration instructions such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The server is bundled with 16.0 GB of memory (4.0 GB per vCPU), 50 GB of local SSD storage, and 1 complimentary public IPv4 address. It does not include any GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results show strong single-threaded compute metrics, including a stress-ng single-core score of 2758.58 and a single-threaded gzip compression rate of 33.57 GB/sec, placing it in the top 25% of evaluated systems. General computational tests yield average results across the board, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 5516.0, a PassMark CPU score of 9273.65, and a multi-core stress-ng result of 9375.63. Memory performance presents notable trade-offs: while small-block cached read bandwidth reaches 563.42 GB/sec, uncached large-block read bandwidth drops to 6.32 GB/sec (bottom 10%), paired with a lower PassMark memory score of 1368.84.

Operationally, the server delivers typical entry-to-mid performance for web and database workloads, achieving 6.19 million Redis SET operations per second and 9.12 GB/sec throughput in static web serving benchmarks. Natural language processing benchmarks handle smaller 135M models adequately at 163.78 tokens per second during generation, but struggle on larger models without dedicated accelerators. Given the balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and entry-level storage capacity, this instance offers functional resource density for general purpose applications, web servers, lightweight databases, and non-concurrent CI/CD pipelines.
description: UpCloud STARTER-4xCPU-16GB is a general-purpose virtual machine in the Starter family powered by a 4-vCPU AMD EPYC 9575F processor running on the KVM hypervisor. Based on the x86_64 architecture, the server provides 16.0 GB of RAM (a standard 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio) and includes 50 GB of bundled local SSD storage along with 1 complimentary public IPv4 address. It does not feature a GPU. Benchmark testing highlights strong single-core compute performance and fast single-threaded compression alongside average multi-core results. However, memory performance exhibits bottlenecks in large uncached read operations. The instance is suited for general purpose workloads, static web serving, intermediate caching, CI/CD runners, and light database deployments.
